name        = "michi-core"

workspace = true

# Audit: Rust best practices, correctness and performance

Base: origin/main at adc8147 (0.10.0). Toolchain: rustc 1.99.1 stable (also 1.93.0 for MSRV). Nothing changed in the repo; scratch crates
live in /private/tmp/claude-501/{ap,gp,sp}.

Overall: this part of the code is in good shape. Rendering is fast (divan, `toon_render`: 44 ns/row at 1000 rows; kv: 29 ns/item), the
pipeline scheduler is linear and cancel-safe by construction, rustdoc is clean, MSRV 1.93 passes, and the wall-time scaling tests did not flake under load.
The findings below are real but mostly small. Only #1 is a measurable hot spot.

## What I ran (and results)

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -W clippy::pedantic -W clippy::nursery` | 394 lines of output; ~80% is `missing_const_for_fn` (118), `assert!(x.is_empty())` in tests (31), `doc_markdown` (27), `pub(crate)` in private module (41), `Duration::from_millis` style (12). Triaged: only the items cited below matter. |
| `cargo +stable doc --workspace --no-deps --all-features` with `RUSTDOCFLAGS=-W rustdoc::all` | 0 warnings, 0 errors |
| `cargo +1.93.0 check --workspace --all-features --all-targets --locked` | passes (CI only checks without `--all-targets`; tests and benches also compile on 1.93) |
| `cargo nextest run --workspace --all-features` | 1141 tests, 11.9 s, all pass |
| Scaling tests under load: 24 `yes` processes on 18 cores, 12 repeated `nextest run --test scaling` for the three crates | 0 / 12 runs failed. Best-of-5 and the 3x margin hold. Not flaky. |
| `cargo bench` (core toon/kv, graph, pipeline scheduler, `--sample-count 30`) | see numbers in findings |
| Allocation counting (global counting allocator, scratch crate `ap`) | see #1 |
| `Send`/`Sync` of `Plan`, `ExecOptions`, `RunRecord`, `ResumeOptions`, `BreakerRegistry`, `CancellationToken`, `ExecutionError`, `StepContext`, `PlanError`, `Dag`, `Graph`, `Violations`, `GraphBuilder`, and the `execute` and `resume` futures (scratch crate `sp`) | all hold (the one compile error was a temporary-lifetime slip in my own test, reported after type-check) |

Bench numbers (median): toon render 1/10/100/1000 rows = 267 ns / 600 ns / 4.3 us / 44.8 us. graph: `validate_chain` 1k = 119 us, 100k = 17 ms;
`validate_layered_10k` (100x100 layers, 990k edges) 124 ms declaration order, 165 ms key order; `report_100k_cycle` 4.2 ms; `ready_and_layers_10k` 560 us.
scheduler (500 steps): sequential 519 us, parallel cap 16 455 us, `validate_plan` 139 us (about 1 us per step, nothing to optimise).

---

## #1 [M] `AgentResponse` deep-clones every row on each validate and each render

Evidence:
- `crates/michi-core/src/response.rs:240`: `section_options` does `ToonOptions::new(name, fields.to_vec(), rows.to_vec())` ("Copies the rows: `ToonOptions` owns them", doc comment above it).
- It is called from `section_part` (:258, once per render), `failed_flags` (:279, called by `is_error()`), and `root_collision` paths, so one `is_error()` plus one `to_call_tool_result()` clones the whole body twice.
- Measured with a counting allocator (scratch crate `ap`; 3 fields, 90-char title cells), release build:

| 1000 rows | time/iter | allocs/iter | bytes/iter |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `render_toon(&opts)` | 70 us | 3 | 138 KB |
| `AgentResponse::render(Text)` | 95 us | 2015 | 393 KB |
| `AgentResponse::is_error()` (documented "validates without rendering") | 27 us | 2011 | 170 KB |
| `AgentResponse::to_call_tool_result()` | 262 us | 2019 | 902 KB |
| `is_error()` + `to_call_tool_result()` | 294 us | 4030 | 1.07 MB |

  At 100 rows: 215 allocs for `render` vs 3 for `render_toon`. About 2 allocations per row come only from the clone (the per-row `Vec` plus the heap `CompactString`s over 24 bytes).

Why it matters: this is the path every MCP tool response takes, and `is_error()` is a validation that allocates a full copy of the data. The time cost is about 35% on `render` and `is_error()` is dominated by it. It also makes peak memory 2-3x the response size.

Change: let `ToonDocument::validate`/`render_parts` work on a borrowed view (`&str` type name, `&[String]` fields, `&[Vec<Value>]` rows, plus the scalar options). `ToonOptions` can build that view from `&self`, and `section_options` becomes a struct of references. Internal change only.

Effort: M. Breaking: no (`ToonDocument` stays opaque; `validate(&ToonOptions)` keeps its signature). Confidence: high (measured).

Related, smaller: `render_parts` capacity guess (`60 + rows * (fields * 12 + 10)`, render.rs ~line 405) was too small for the bench data above (138 KB allocated for a 100 KB result, so it grew). Cheap to improve by summing string lengths, but not worth a finding on its own.

## #2 [M] Observer callbacks and `record_start` run synchronously on the scheduler task

Evidence: `crates/michi-pipeline/src/scheduler.rs` `drive()` calls `self.record_start(durable, i)` (and `observe(... on_step_started)`) inline inside the dispatch `while` loop, and `set_terminal` calls `on_step_finished` inline. `DurableObserver::record_start` (exec.rs:85-93) exists specifically to persist a marker before the step may run, i.e. file or DB I/O. The docs say "Keep it quick" (exec.rs:44) but the one trait whose purpose is durable persistence cannot be quick.

Why it matters: with `durable_starts`, steps start serially, each waiting on a blocking write, on a Tokio worker thread. On a `current_thread` runtime, one slow fsync stalls every in-flight step's timeout and cancellation handling. N parallel steps start in N x fsync, not 1 x fsync. Not measured (needs a slow observer), so treat the severity as a code-reading judgment.

Change: either make `record_start` async (`fn record_start<'a>(&'a self, ...) -> Pin<Box<dyn Future<Output = Result<(), String>> + Send + 'a>>`) and await it inside the spawned task before the first attempt, or run it via `spawn_blocking` and document that the scheduler waits. The finish observer should stay sync but document the same limit.

Effort: M. Breaking: yes (trait signature) but all consumers are our own repos, pre-1.0. Confidence: medium (design reading, no measurement).

## #3 [L] No compile-time `Send + Sync` assertions in `michi-pipeline` and `michi-graph`

Evidence: `michi-core/src/lib.rs:147-209` has `assert_send_sync_static` for its public types; `grep assert_send` finds nothing in the other two crates. I checked by compiling that all the types above are `Send + Sync` and that `execute`/`resume` futures are `Send` (a scratch crate), so this is a guard gap, not a bug. A future `Rc`/`Cell`/`MutexGuard`-across-await change in `scheduler.rs` would silently make `tokio::spawn(execute(..))` stop compiling for consumers.

Change: add a test with `fn is_send<T: Send>(_: &T)` over the `execute`/`resume` futures and `assert_send_sync` over the public types, in both crates. Effort: S. Breaking: no. Confidence: high.

## #4 [L] Source-text scanning tests stand in for compile-time guarantees

Evidence: `crates/michi-core/src/toon/render.rs` `sole_constructor_for_toon_document` (~line 1058 onward) plus helpers `strip_test_modules` and `find_closing_line`, justified by a ~45-line doc comment on `mod proof` (render.rs ~line 232-280). Its own comment says Rust field privacy already enforces the guarantee. Other `include_str!` source greps: `toon/mod.rs` `must_use_and_list_signature_match_the_spec` asserts `src.contains("#[must_use]\n    pub fn new(")` (a rustfmt change breaks it, a wrong `#[must_use]` placement does not). 7 `include_str!("mod.rs"/"render.rs")` uses in `michi-core/src`.

Why it matters: these assert on formatting, not behaviour (they can fail for the wrong reason and pass while the property is broken, e.g. the macro case it admits it cannot see), and they cost maintenance. The repo already has `trybuild` (`tests/ui-fail/`), which proves the privacy property with the real compiler.

Change: replace with a `compile_fail` doctest or a trybuild case ("`ToonDocument { opts }` outside `proof` does not compile", "`ToonDocument::validate` is the only constructor"), keep the privacy argument as a 3-line comment, drop the scanner. Effort: S. Breaking: no. Confidence: medium-high.

## #5 [L] `michi-graph` claims `no_std` but is only built for the host

Evidence: `crates/michi-graph/src/builder.rs:21-28` uses `core::sync::atomic::AtomicUsize::fetch_add` (`NEXT_BUILDER`). That does not exist on targets without atomic read-modify-write (for example `thumbv6m-none-eabi`). No CI job builds the crate for a bare-metal target; `#![no_std]` on a host build proves only that no `std::` path is used. I could not check a target: only `wasm32-*` is listed by `rustup target list --installed`, and `cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` failed with E0463 (core not installed for that toolchain) so this is **unverified**.

Change: add `cargo check -p michi-graph --target thumbv7m-none-eabi` (and, if the claim should cover cortex-m0, `thumbv6m`) to CI; if the cortex-m0 case matters, replace the global counter with a per-builder identity that needs no RMW (for example the address of an `Arc` allocated by the builder). Effort: S. Breaking: no. Confidence: low-medium (the code reading is certain; whether anyone targets such chips is not).

## #6 [L] Graph `build` is the dominant cost of `Dag::from_nodes` at large edge counts

Evidence: scratch timing (release, 100x100 fully connected layers, 990k edges, `String` keys): `GraphBuilder::build` 96 ms, `validate` 30 ms, `layers()` 0.9 ms. `build` (`builder.rs:131-165`) resolves each prerequisite with a binary search over `String` keys (about 13 string compares per edge) and then runs four stable sorts over the edge vector (`resolved.sort_by` on a 4-tuple, `dedup_by`, `sort_by_key(seq)`, and the same for `dangling`). That is about 100 ns/edge. Linear-ish (n log n), so not a scaling problem; consumers' graphs are far smaller than this (the bench itself says "beyond real dependency graphs").

Change (only if it ever matters): dedup via one sort of indices instead of sorting the edges twice, and memoise the lookup of the previous prerequisite key for runs of the same target. Likely 1.5-2x, unmeasured. Effort: S. Breaking: no. Confidence: high that it is a constant factor only.

## #7 [L] `toon::list` holds three copies of the data at once

Evidence: `crates/michi-core/src/toon/mod.rs:297-340`. Each item goes `serde_json::to_vec` -> `from_slice` into an `serde_json::Map` (kept in `objects`, with `preserve_order`), and then a second pass builds `Vec<Vec<Value>>` rows, and only then renders. Peak memory is roughly JSON tree + `Value` rows + output. The round trip through text is deliberate (comment about `f32`), so the intent is fine; the retention of `objects` until all rows are built is what can be avoided. Not measured (memory), so **unverified**.

Change: only the field-union needs a first pass; either keep the serialized `Vec<u8>` per item (cheaper than a `Map`) and parse twice, or convert to `Vec<Value>` per item immediately with a growing field map and pad rows at the end. Effort: M. Breaking: no. Confidence: medium.

## #8 [L] Missing derives and conversions on small public types

Evidence (clippy `derive_partial_eq_without_eq` at `michi-core/src/hints.rs:2` and `michi-pipeline/src/record.rs:10`; the rest by reading):
- `Hint` (`hints.rs:2-5`) derives `Debug, Clone, PartialEq` but not `Eq`, `Hash`, `Ord`, and has no `AsRef<str>`. `AgentResponse` dedups hints with `Vec::contains` (response.rs ~line 345), which a `Hash`/`Eq` would let callers do with a set.
- `AttemptRecord` (record.rs:10) can be `Eq` (u32, Option<enum>, Option<String>, Duration).
- `StepId`/`RunId` (`id.rs`, macro) have `Display`, `AsRef<str>`, `TryFrom`, `Hash`, `Ord` but no `FromStr` (so `"x".parse::<StepId>()` and clap/serde-adjacent parsing need `try_new`) and no `Borrow<str>`, so a `BTreeMap<StepId, _>` cannot be looked up by `&str`.
- `#[inline]` appears twice in all three crates; that is fine for LTO builds, not a finding.

Change: add the derives and the `FromStr`/`Borrow<str>` impls. Effort: S. Breaking: no (additive). Confidence: high.

## #9 [L] `pub` napi-core functions take owned arguments they do not consume

Evidence: clippy `needless_pass_by_value` at `crates/michi-core/src/napi.rs:238` (`empty_state(type_name: String)`), `:489` (`render_already_done(operation: String, summary: String, hints: Vec<String>)`), `:500` (`render_domain_error`), `:592`. These are the "Rust-typed core" re-exported as `michi_core::napi::*`. The `#[napi]` wrappers need owned values from JS, but the inner functions only read them and then drop them.

Why it matters: negligible time; it is an API-shape smell on a pub surface (callers must clone to keep their data). Change: take `&str`/`&[String]` in the inner functions and borrow from the napi wrapper. Effort: S. Breaking: yes for Rust callers of `michi_core::napi::*` (probably none). Confidence: medium.

## #10 [L] Benchmark and scaling coverage gaps

- Benches: only `toon::render_toon`, `kv`, graph and the scheduler. Nothing covers `AgentResponse` (multi-section envelope, `to_call_tool_result`, JSON render), `toon::list` (serde), `DomainError` rendering/redaction, or `truncate*`. #1 above went unnoticed for that reason.
- Scaling tests (`michi-core/tests/scaling.rs`): `render_toon` rows and cell length, kv items, `truncate`, `truncate_by_size`, envelope section count. Missing: `AgentResponse` rows per section, `toon::list` item count, many cut cells (the `cut` vector and `truncated` block), `render_hints` with many hints, redaction on long strings. I did not find a quadratic path in these by reading `push_list`/`push_truncated`/`truncated_table`; this is coverage, not a bug.

Change: add an `AgentResponse::render` + `to_call_tool_result` divan bench with an allocation-count assertion (a counted-allocs test is deterministic, unlike wall time) and the missing scaling cases. Effort: S. Breaking: no. Confidence: high.

---

## Considered and not reported (checked, nothing to fix)

- `Value::from(String)` uses `CompactString::new(s)`; I suspected an extra copy. Measured: 1 allocation for a 200-byte `String` either way. No change needed. `size_of::<Value>() == 24`.
- `Vec<Vec<Value>>` vs a flat layout: render cost is 44 ns/row and dominated by formatting; the per-row `Vec` only costs on the caller's build side and on the clone in #1, which goes away with a borrowed view. A flat layout would break the public `rows` field for no measured gain.
- Pipeline cancel safety: `attempt_once`/`precheck_once` race the step against the token with `select! { biased; .. }` and drop the losing future; `JoinSet` is owned by `drive()` so dropping `execute` aborts all steps; `spawn_blocking` closures cannot be aborted and are guarded by the `IN_FLIGHT` set, the intended trade-off (documented in blocking.rs). `AdmissionGuard` releases a half-open probe on `Drop`, so a panic in a step does not wedge a breaker. No `MutexGuard` is held across an await (confirmed by the `Send` check).
- Tokio feature use: library needs `time`, `rt`, `macros`; it uses `JoinSet`, `spawn_blocking`, `select!` and `tokio::time`, all covered; `rt-multi-thread` is dev-only. Fine.
- Default dependency set: `michi-core` default = `thiserror` + `compact_str` as the docs say; `michi-graph` has none.
- michi-graph `usize as u32` casts flagged by pedantic (`algo.rs:118,182,189,200`): safe because `GraphBuilder::node` caps nodes at `u32::MAX - 1` and sets `overflow`. Not worth `try_from`.
- `BreakerRegistry` and `IN_FLIGHT` grow with the number of distinct keys and are never evicted; keys come from plan authors, so bounded in practice.
- Wall-time scaling tests: robust (see table). No change.

## Not examined

- `crates/michi-core/src/napi.rs` beyond its signatures (3037 lines; the numeric-boundary and row-accounting work is covered by other agents) and the Node-side build; `napi` feature performance (FFI marshalling cost) not measured.
- `error.rs` (1240 lines), `redact.rs`, `resilience.rs` (backoff maths) for performance; only read for derives.
- No flamegraph or `dhat` run (allocation counting with a custom allocator was enough to localise #1).
- Cross-target builds (`thumbv6m`, `wasm32`) because the targets are not installed; no `cargo miri` or `loom` runs for the pipeline's `Mutex` and `JoinSet` interplay.
- Fuzz targets under `fuzz/` (nightly only) and the `evals/` directory.

- Memory use of `toon::list` and the graph (#6, #7 are time or code reading only for memory).

That is about 100 ns/edge. Linear-ish (n log n), so not a scaling problem; consumers' graphs are far smaller than this (the bench itself says "beyond real dependency graphs").

Change (only if it ever matters): dedup via one sort of indices instead of sorting the edges twice, and memoise the lookup of the previous prerequisite key for runs of the same target. Likely 1.5-2x, unmeasured. Effort: S. Breaking: no. Confidence: high that it is a constant factor only.

## #7 [L] `toon::list` holds three copies of the data at once

Evidence: `crates/michi-core/src/toon/mod.rs:297-340`. Each item goes `serde_json::to_vec` -> `from_slice` into an `serde_json::Map` (kept in `objects`, with `preserve_order`), and then a second pass builds `Vec<Vec<Value>>` rows, and only then renders. Peak memory is roughly JSON tree + `Value` rows + output. The round trip through text is deliberate (comment about `f32`), so the intent is fine; the retention of `objects` until all rows are built is what can be avoided. Not measured (memory), so **unverified**.

Change: only the field-union needs a first pass; either keep the serialized `Vec<u8>` per item (cheaper than a `Map`) and parse twice, or convert to `Vec<Value>` per item immediately with a growing field map and pad rows at the end. Effort: M. Breaking: no. Confidence: medium.

## #8 [L] Missing derives and conversions on small public types

Evidence (clippy `derive_partial_eq_without_eq` at `michi-core/src/hints.rs:2` and `michi-pipeline/src/record.rs:10`; the rest by reading):
- `Hint` (`hints.rs:2-5`) derives `Debug, Clone, PartialEq` but not `Eq`, `Hash`, `Ord`, and has no `AsRef<str>`. `AgentResponse` dedups hints with `Vec::contains` (response.rs ~line 345), which a `Hash`/`Eq` would let callers do with a set.
- `AttemptRecord` (record.rs:10) can be `Eq` (u32, Option<enum>, Option<String>, Duration).
- `StepId`/`RunId` (`id.rs`, macro) have `Display`, `AsRef<str>`, `TryFrom`, `Hash`, `Ord` but no `FromStr` (so `"x".parse::<StepId>()` and clap/serde-adjacent parsing need `try_new`) and no `Borrow<str>`, so a `BTreeMap<StepId, _>` cannot be looked up by `&str`.
- `#[inline]` appears twice in all three crates; that is fine for LTO builds, not a finding.

Change: add the derives and the `FromStr`/`Borrow<str>` impls. Effort: S. Breaking: no (additive). Confidence: high.

## #9 [L] `pub` napi-core functions take owned arguments they do not consume

Evidence: clippy `needless_pass_by_value` at `crates/michi-core/src/napi.rs:238` (`empty_state(type_name: String)`), `:489` (`render_already_done(operation: String, summary: String, hints: Vec<String>)`), `:500` (`render_domain_error`), `:592`. These are the "Rust-typed core" re-exported as `michi_core::napi::*`. The `#[napi]` wrappers need owned values from JS, but the inner functions only read them and then drop them.

Why it matters: negligible time; it is an API-shape smell on a pub surface (callers must clone to keep their data). Change: take `&str`/`&[String]` in the inner functions and borrow from the napi wrapper. Effort: S. Breaking: yes for Rust callers of `michi_core::napi::*` (probably none). Confidence: medium.

## #10 [L] Benchmark and scaling coverage gaps

- Benches: only `toon::render_toon`, `kv`, graph and the scheduler. Nothing covers `AgentResponse` (multi-section envelope, `to_call_tool_result`, JSON render), `toon::list` (serde), `DomainError` rendering/redaction, or `truncate*`. #1 above went unnoticed for that reason.
- Scaling tests (`michi-core/tests/scaling.rs`): `render_toon` rows and cell length, kv items, `truncate`, `truncate_by_size`, envelope section count. Missing: `AgentResponse` rows per section, `toon::list` item count, many cut cells (the `cut` vector and `truncated` block), `render_hints` with many hints, redaction on long strings. I did not find a quadratic path in these by reading `push_list`/`push_truncated`/`truncated_table`; this is coverage, not a bug.

Change: add an `AgentResponse::render` + `to_call_tool_result` divan bench with an allocation-count assertion (a counted-allocs test is deterministic, unlike wall time) and the missing scaling cases. Effort: S. Breaking: no. Confidence: high.

---

## Considered and not reported (checked, nothing to fix)

- `Value::from(String)` uses `CompactString::new(s)`; I suspected an extra copy. Measured: 1 allocation for a 200-byte `String` either way. No change needed. `size_of::<Value>() == 24`.
- `Vec<Vec<Value>>` vs a flat layout: render cost is 44 ns/row and dominated by formatting; the per-row `Vec` only costs on the caller's build side and on the clone in #1, which goes away with a borrowed view. A flat layout would break the public `rows` field for no measured gain.
- Pipeline cancel safety: `attempt_once`/`precheck_once` race the step against the token with `select! { biased; .. }` and drop the losing future; `JoinSet` is owned by `drive()` so dropping `execute` aborts all steps; `spawn_blocking` closures cannot be aborted and are guarded by the `IN_FLIGHT` set, the intended trade-off (documented in blocking.rs). `AdmissionGuard` releases a half-open probe on `Drop`, so a panic in a step does not wedge a breaker. No `MutexGuard` is held across an await (confirmed by the `Send` check).
- Tokio feature use: library needs `time`, `rt`, `macros`; it uses `JoinSet`, `spawn_blocking`, `select!` and `tokio::time`, all covered; `rt-multi-thread` is dev-only. Fine.
- Default dependency set: `michi-core` default = `thiserror` + `compact_str` as the docs say; `michi-graph` has none.
- michi-graph `usize as u32` casts flagged by pedantic (`algo.rs:118,182,189,200`): safe because `GraphBuilder::node` caps nodes at `u32::MAX - 1` and sets `overflow`. Not worth `try_from`.
- `BreakerRegistry` and `IN_FLIGHT` grow with the number of distinct keys and are never evicted; keys come from plan authors, so bounded in practice.
- Wall-time scaling tests: robust (see table). No change.

## Not examined

- `crates/michi-core/src/napi.rs` beyond its signatures (3037 lines; the numeric-boundary and row-accounting work is covered by other agents) and the Node-side build; `napi` feature performance (FFI marshalling cost) not measured.
- `error.rs` (1240 lines), `redact.rs`, `resilience.rs` (backoff maths) for performance; only read for derives.
- No flamegraph or `dhat` run (allocation counting with a custom allocator was enough to localise #1).
- Cross-target builds (`thumbv6m`, `wasm32`) because the targets are not installed; no `cargo miri` or `loom` runs for the pipeline's `Mutex` and `JoinSet` interplay.
- Fuzz targets under `fuzz/` (nightly only) and the `evals/` directory.
- Memory use of `toon::list` and the graph (#6, #7 are time or code reading only for memory).
